verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough and runny nose starting “maybe five or six days ago” and describes the cough as dry: “this…cough for quite a few days, and my nose is running… I think it started… maybe five or six days ago”; “It’s quite dry”.
Patient describes “this…cough… It’s just so continuous… It’s quite dry and it’s just all day. Like, keeps me up at night as well” indicating a dry, continuous cough worse at night disturbing sleep.

Patient states, “the coughing is giving me a sore throat… Just my throat is irritated from coughing, but it’s not that bad when I swallow or anything,” indicating sore throat from coughing without pain on swallowing.
Doctor notes “my nose is running” and patient confirms runny nose; rhinorrhea is the medical term for runny nose.

Patient reports chills and probable fever without measurement: “I’ve been having, like, shivers… I haven’t taken my temperature. So I’m not 100% sure if I had a fever, but feels like I probably did… I kept adding more sweaters on, and I was still cold.”
Patient reports diffuse muscle aches: “my muscle was really hurting… Especially, like, in my arms, my legs, like, just everywhere,” consistent with diffuse myalgias in arms and legs.

Patient describes feeling lethargic and weak: “I feel, you know, generally tired… So to be honest, all I feel like doing is just lying in bed.” Clinician summarizes: “Basically getting quite lethargic and weak.” Patient agrees: “Yeah, pretty much.”
On breathing, patient says, “I don’t think so… I don’t feel breathless, no.” This supports denial of shortness of breath at rest.
When asked, “Any pain in your chest?”, patient responds, “No, not that either,” denying chest pain.
Clinician asks, “How are your ears? Your ears feel blocked?… No pain or discharge?” Patient responds, “No, they feel okay, actually. Yeah… Not pain on the ears?” indicating no ear pain or discharge.
When asked about appetite patient replies, “I mean, it’s okay… I had a little bit of diarrhea, but it didn’t cut my appetite or anything,” indicating appetite is okay.

Patient explains, “at the beginning… I had a little bit of diarrhea… Has it got better now, the diarrhea? Yeah, yeah, it got better. It was only like, the first… It started at the same time as the cough started, and then it stopped,” indicating transient diarrhea at onset now resolved.
Clinician asks, “have you had any nausea? Have you had any vomiting?” Patient replies, “No, no. No nausea, no vomiting.”
When asked about “waterworks… your urine,” patient replies, “Oh, no, no, no. That’s fine… You’re passing urine. Okay,” indicating denial of urinary symptoms.
Patient states, “Well, I have type 2 diabetes.”
Patient states, “I have quite high blood pressure,” indicating hypertension.
Patient says, “I take Metformin for the diabetes.”
Patient says, “And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure.”
Clinician asks, “Any allergies at all to medication?” Patient replies, “No allergies, no,” indicating no known drug allergies.
Patient states, “My dad also has type 2 diabetes.”

On social situation patient says, “Just. It’s just me and my partner.” When asked, “Is your partner well at the moment?” patient replies, “Yeah. He has none of this… He’s fine,” indicating a well partner.
Patient says, “I am a developer.” Clinician clarifies, “So you work in the IT field. Okay.”
Clinician asks, “Do you smoke at all, April?” Patient replies, “I used to, but I’ve stopped for about six months now,” indicating ex-smoker quit ~6 months ago.
Regarding alcohol, patient says, “I don’t drink more than like, say, three evenings a week… Wine, mostly… maybe two or three glasses,” matching 2–3 glasses wine up to 3 evenings/week.

Clinician summarizes: “I think essentially I think you’re going through a bit of a viral illness… you’ve had a bit of a cough, bit of a runny nose, feeling quite weak and lethargic.” History includes 5–6 days of dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, no breathlessness or chest pain, and resolved initial diarrhea as documented earlier. This supports assessment of acute viral/URTI based on those features.

Patient: “Well, I have type 2 diabetes… Should I say I take Metformin for the diabetes?” Later: “I have it under control, and since I’ve started taking this medication, I’ve just been regularly checking that it’s under control,” indicating diabetes managed with metformin and reported controlled.

Patient: “I have quite high blood pressure… And I take Lisinopril for the high blood pressure… I have it under control… regularly checking that it’s under control,” indicating hypertension managed with lisinopril and reported as controlled.

Alcohol history shows moderate use. Clinician responds: “you’re probably just about under the limit… maybe something that you can maybe cut down on if you can… just because of your blood pressure and diabetes,” indicating moderate use and counseling to reduce due to HTN and diabetes.
Clinician advises for this illness: “things you can do to help yourself in the meantime is to get some nice rest,” which is rest for the acute viral illness.
Clinician advises, “drink plenty of fluids, keep yourself well hydrated,” i.e., increase fluid intake for the current illness.
Clinician: “You can take regular paracetamol,” referring to symptom relief for this acute illness.
Regarding work: “I would say maybe take a day or two off work if you can get some good bed rest, and maybe think about work early next week,” which corresponds to considering 1–2 days off work.
Clinician: “I’m hoping that… you’re probably over the worst of it now. It’s been five days… Normally last about a week to 10 days,” stating an expected 7–10 day course.
Clinician: “If you feel like it’s still any better in two to three days, it’s probably worth coming back to see me again,” meaning return in 2–3 days if not improved.
Clinician: “if your cough isn’t getting any better or your breathing is getting worse, I want you to come back and see me sooner,” advising earlier return if breathing worsens / SOB develops.

Clinician: “if you are still feeling feverish and your cough isn’t getting any better, then we may look to give you some antibiotics for your chest,” indicating consideration of chest antibiotics at review if still febrile and no improvement.

Transcript notes ongoing metformin use and routine check-ups: “I just regularly go see a doctor that just checks up on it,” but there is no explicit plan stated in this consult to continue metformin or specific instruction about routine follow-up; that is background, not a new plan item.

Similarly, ongoing lisinopril and routine checks are described historically: “Same with the high blood pressure… regularly checking that it’s under control,” but no explicit plan is made in this visit to continue lisinopril or schedule routine follow-up.

Clinician counsels: “maybe something that you can maybe cut down on if you can… maybe for the first few weeks. Why don’t you cut down to two glasses a week and then one week thereafter. And if you are coping okay, then we can maybe try and cut down altogether,” matching the described alcohol reduction plan.

Clinician advises, “if your cough isn’t getting any better or your breathing is getting worse, I want you to come back and see me sooner,” i.e., return sooner if breathing worsens / SOB develops.
